scope: Six separately executed single-file runs, once each, sequentially, with one Vitest worker. Concurrent parent PostgreSQL lane remained active, so these are not machine-wide idle-isolation runs.
configuration: Default test assertions and timeouts retained. No automatic retries, dependencies, application configuration, fixture configuration, or product/test source changes.
environment: Node 24 directory prepended to child PATH. AOA_RUN_WIN_INTEGRATION, AOA_D1_LIVE, E2B_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL, AOA_HOME, AOA_CONFIG removed from child environment.
commandsAndLogs: isolated-summary.json contains complete argv arrays, cwd, UTC timestamps, exit codes, file/test counts, durations, and absolute log paths for each run.
sandboxStartupAttempts: All six initial sandbox attempts exited 1 before test collection because esbuild could not read the existing repository config (Access is denied). These are infrastructure startup failures, not assertion attempts. Preserved separately in sandbox-startup-*.log and sandbox-startup-isolated-summary.json. Actual assertion runs used approved escalation.

results.demonstrated: createRequire(import.meta.url) in test:40-41 cannot resolve playwright-core/package.json. Browser-runtime declares playwright as a devDependency, not playwright-core. Resolution probe confirms playwright 1.59.1 resolves, and its own require resolves transitive playwright-core 1.59.1 in pnpm's package store, but direct require from the test yields MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
results.rootCause: Direct transitive dependency lookup is not exposed from this package in the installed pnpm layout. No version mismatch was demonstrated.

results.classification: Original full-run 5000ms timeout did not reproduce
results.demonstrated: First test took 4121ms; subsequent tests took 315ms and 305ms. First test resets modules then dynamically imports client.ts, which statically imports Drizzle, postgres, and the full schema.
results.hypothesis: Cold import/transform cost and execution load can consume the 5-second budget; import cost has not been instrumented and machine-wide contention is not proven as root cause.
results.limitation: Single-file pass does not erase original 5018ms timeout.

results.demonstrated: beforeAll at 170 did not finish await import('../app.js') within 30000ms. Runtime worker-denial/positive-control tests passed. Missing cloud-composition-does-not-exist.cjs child error is the intentional positive control, not this failure.
results.unresolved: The timeout alone does not distinguish a slow import graph from an ESM-cycle stall. Test comments describe an existing Drizzle require(esm) cycle, but no such cycle error was produced by this timed-out hook.

results.classification: Original full-run 30000ms timeout did not reproduce
results.demonstrated: Previously failing static-context test took 18248ms, versus 31501ms in original run. Authority-writer inventory took 56496ms, versus 102451ms originally. Source implements synchronous TypeScript AST parsing/walks over adversarial fixtures and production code. Vitest duration 113.03s.
results.hypothesis: Expensive synchronous analysis is sensitive to execution conditions. Exact source of original slowdown has not been measured.
results.limitation: Single-file pass does not erase original failure.

results.classification: Original UI failure did not reproduce
results.demonstrated: Archive test passed 125ms. Original full-run log shows the synchronous getByTestId immediately before click could not find archive-workspace-ws-1 and the DOM contained loading skeletons. Test waits for both archive buttons before that synchronous re-query.
results.hypothesis: A render/loading-state transition between awaited readiness and synchronous re-query is consistent with the original evidence; the trigger and underlying React/query scheduling cause remain unproven.
results.limitation: Single-file pass does not erase original failure.

results.classification: Original queued unhandled rejection did not reproduce; a different assertion failed
results.demonstrated: STALLED upload test at 487 expected WireProtocolError but received ResourceNotAvailableError, 27ms. It starts export and destroy concurrently at 485-486. Queued deadline test passed 410ms. No unhandled rejection or PromiseRejectionHandledWarning appeared in this single-file log.
results.newFailureHypothesis: Concurrent destroy may acquire the sandbox operation path before export inspection, causing resource-unavailable refusal; request arrival/lock order was not instrumented, so this remains a hypothesis.
results.originalUnhandledEvidence: Original full-run log reports WireProtocolError for queued test and PromiseRejectionHandledWarning. Test creates both first and queued promises at 692-700, awaits first's rejection at 701, then attaches queued's rejection assertion at 704. Source therefore leaves queued temporarily without a rejection handler; a queued response arriving first can produce the observed late-handler symptom. Timing order was not demonstrated in the single-file run.
results.limitation: The newly observed assertion failure is separate from the original full-run unhandled error. Neither was fixed or retried.

verification: git status --short and git diff --stat were empty after the six runs, and git rev-parse HEAD remained the requested pinned SHA. No full suite, typecheck, or build was rerun because this task was limited to six targeted reproductions.
